successCriteria.description: The controller class accepts ILeaveRequestService in its constructor and exposes one handler method per service operation (createDraft, submit, approve, reject, cancel, findById, findByEmployeeId, query) — 8 methods total, each returning a plain JSON-serializable object with Date fields converted to ISO 8601 strings.

The routes plugin registers exactly 8 endpoints covering all service operations: createDraft, submit, approve, reject, cancel, findById, findByEmployeeId, and query. The employee-specific route is registered before the parameterized :id route to prevent route collision.

Every service error code is mapped to the correct HTTP status: REQUEST_NOT_FOUND/EMPLOYEE_NOT_FOUND/POLICY_NOT_FOUND/BALANCE_NOT_FOUND → 404, INVALID_DATE_RANGE/MINIMUM_NOTICE_VIOLATION → 400, INVALID_STATE_TRANSITION → 409, NOT_MANAGER → 403, INSUFFICIENT_BALANCE/BALANCE_CLOSED/POLICY_INACTIVE → 409, and any unrecognized error → 500.
The routes plugin is registered in src/app.ts via app.register(leaveRequestRoutes), making all leave-request endpoints available on the Fastify instance.

The route test file uses Fastify's inject() method with a mocked ILeaveRequestService, covering at minimum: a successful createDraft call, a 404 from findById when the service returns null, a 409 from an invalid state transition, and a 200 with empty array from query/findByEmployeeId.

constraints: The controller must not contain any business logic — it delegates entirely to ILeaveRequestService. Its sole responsibilities are: extracting parameters from the request, calling the service method, formatting the response (Date → ISO string), and catching/re-mapping errors to HTTP responses.

The routes plugin must be a standard Fastify plugin (exported async function receiving FastifyInstance). It must instantiate the controller with a real or injected ILeaveRequestService — the wiring strategy (direct instantiation vs. dependency injection) is left to the code agent, but the controller must receive the service interface, not a concrete class.
outOfScope: Authentication and authorization middleware (RBAC enforcement via requireRole guard) — deferred to a later phase. The controller and routes in this phase do not inspect request.user or enforce role checks.
Request body and query parameter validation (GP-003) — the controller in this phase passes DTOs directly to the service without schema validation. Validation middleware or decorators are deferred.

ambiguities.description: The controller reads `request.body` and casts it to a DTO type. At runtime, `request.body` could be `null`, `undefined`, or a non-object primitive. The code agent must decide whether the controller should check that `request.body` is a non-null object before destructuring it into a DTO, or whether to let a runtime TypeError propagate (which the catch block would map to 500).
options: Let TypeError propagate — the catch block maps it to 500
Guard with a null check and return 400 if body is not an object

entityInvariants.invariant: The controller MUST NOT contain any business logic, state-machine enforcement, or direct repository access. It delegates all operations to ILeaveRequestService and only handles HTTP concerns: parameter extraction, response formatting, and error-to-HTTP-status mapping.

All Date fields (startDate, endDate, approvedAt, cancelledAt, createdAt, updatedAt) in HTTP responses MUST be serialized as ISO 8601 strings. The controller is responsible for this transformation; the service returns Date objects.

interfaceConstraints.authRule: Deferred — no auth enforcement in this phase
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Service errors EMPLOYEE_NOT_FOUND, POLICY_NOT_FOUND → 404; POLICY_INACTIVE, INVALID_DATE_RANGE → 400; unexpected → 500
